questions.stem: Which list matches the ten pieces of bridge equipment named in the Bridge Watch Rating standard?
options: Gyro repeater, rate-of-turn indicator, radar, electronic chart, AIS, echo sounder, steering position, autopilot, GPS and VHF radio
Magnetic compass, barometer, radar, paper chart, AIS, log, steering position, sextant, GPS and VHF radio
Gyro repeater, radar, electronic chart, AIS, echo sounder, searchlight, whistle, autopilot, GPS and EPIRB
Rate-of-turn indicator, radar, anemometer, AIS, echo sounder, steering position, autopilot, GPS, NAVTEX and VHF radio
questions.explanation: The standard names these ten items. A rating is not in charge of navigation but is expected to know what each is for and to report when one looks wrong.

questions.stem: What is the relationship between a gyro-compass and a gyro repeater?
options: The repeater finds north by itself and the gyro-compass copies it
The repeater is a magnetic compass corrected for variation
The two are independent, so they can never disagree
The repeater is a dial that copies the heading of the gyro-compass elsewhere, so it can only be as right as the gyro behind it
questions.explanation: The gyro-compass is the source and the repeater is a copy. If the repeater loses step with the gyro it will be wrong, which is why you compare it with the magnetic compass regularly.

questions.stem: Under the Navigation Safety Regulations, 2020, which vessel must have a gyro-compass heading repeater at the emergency steering position?
options: Any vessel of 150 GT or more on any voyage
A vessel of 300 GT or more, but only in restricted visibility
A vessel of 500 GT or more on a voyage other than sheltered waters
Only a vessel of 50 000 GT or more
questions.explanation: Section 111(c)(ii) sets 500 GT or more, other than on sheltered-waters voyages. The 150 GT figure belongs to GNSS and the 50 000 GT figure belongs to the rate-of-turn indicator.

questions.stem: A rate-of-turn indicator reads 15 degrees per minute. How long does a turn of 90 degrees take at that rate?
options: 1.5 minutes
6 minutes
9 minutes
15 minutes
questions.explanation: Time is angle divided by rate: 90 / 15 = 6 minutes. The instrument also tells you the turn has started, is steady and has stopped, before the compass shows it.

questions.stem: From what size of vessel do the regulations require a rate-of-turn indicator?
options: 50 000 GT or more
300 GT or more
500 GT or more
10 000 GT or more
questions.explanation: Section 114(a) sets 50 000 GT. Radar and echo sounder start at 300 GT, and the heading repeater at the emergency steering position starts at 500 GT.

questions.stem: A vessel of 300 GT or more must carry which pair of items under section 110?
options: A 3-GHz radar and an ECDIS
A rate-of-turn indicator and a gyro repeater
An AIS Class B and a GNSS receiver only
A 9-GHz radar and an echo sounder
questions.explanation: Section 110 names the echo sounder and the 9-GHz radar at 300 GT. ECDIS and the rate-of-turn indicator come in under different sections and size limits.

questions.stem: A ship has an AIS Class A and a gyro-compass both fitted. What must be true about their connection?
options: They must be kept separate so a fault in one cannot affect the other
The AIS must take heading from the GPS course over ground
They must be connected so that the AIS transmits heading
No connection is required, because AIS never sends heading
questions.explanation: Section 118(4) requires the connection. Course over ground from a GPS is not heading and should not be used as one.

questions.stem: From what size of vessel must a GNSS receiver be carried, and where does an automatic distress alert get its position?
options: 300 GT or more, and the alert takes its position from the radar
150 GT or more, and the alert takes its position from the GNSS receiver
500 GT or more, and the alert takes its position from the gyro-compass
50 GT or more, and the alert carries no position
questions.explanation: Section 109(1)(a) sets 150 GT and section 221 puts the GNSS position into the distress alert. GPS is one GNSS.

questions.stem: What do the regulations require for a VHF radiotelephone on the bridge?
options: It must be accessible from the conning position, with channel selection possible from there
It must be fitted in the radio room only
It must be able to transmit only on channel 16
It must be switched off while under way in fog
questions.explanation: Section 220 requires access from the conning position so the person conning can use the radio without leaving the watch position.

questions.stem: Which reading must be displayed at the main steering position?
options: The GPS course over ground only
The AIS target list
The echo sounder depth
The standard magnetic compass reading
questions.explanation: Section 106(1) requires the standard magnetic compass reading at the main steering position. Separately, on vessels 55 m or more built on or after 1 July 2002, section 140 sets a field of vision of at least 60 degrees each side of right ahead.

questions.stem: The ship is in restricted visibility with the autopilot on. What must the arrangements allow?
options: Changeover only after the engine room has been told, with no helmsman needed
Changeover made by a rating on his own judgement, with the autopilot kept on for as long as possible
An immediate changeover to manual steering, with a qualified helmsman available, made by or under the supervision of the person in charge of the deck watch
No changeover, because the autopilot is safer than a helmsman in fog
questions.explanation: Section 133 requires immediate changeover to manual steering, a qualified helmsman available, and changeover by or under the supervision of the person in charge of the deck watch.

questions.stem: The radar shows nothing ahead in fog, but you can hear a horn. What does Rule 5 expect you to do?
options: Disregard the sound until the radar confirms it
Keep the look-out by sight and hearing as well as by all available means, and report the sound
Report only if the AIS shows a vessel
Let the autopilot decide whether to alter course
questions.explanation: Rule 5 requires a proper look-out by sight and hearing and by all available means. Electronic aids support the look-out and never replace it.
